mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (exceeding 0.3 percentage points in three months) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities as corporate revenue expectations are revised downward, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases (i.e., when both series decline, returns are positive in >60% of instances).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY change > 2.5%), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust economic activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 50,000 in a single month signals weakening economic conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS falls > 50k in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a severe economic slowdown, which triggers a significant sell-off in equities, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in GDPC1 and HOUST fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of rising interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%), the S&P 500 tends to underperform as higher borrowing costs dampen corporate investment and consumer spending, leading to negative 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.
